blog_summary: Adrian Colyer summarizes Szekeres et al.'s 2013 paper as a comprehensive 'Systematization of Knowledge' (SoK) on memory corruption attacks and defenses. The blog highlights the complexity of defending against these attacks, especially given space and time overhead constraints. The paper emphasizes that the best solution is using type-safe languages, but acknowledges the impracticality of rewriting existing C/C++ code. Colyer notes the paper's excellent conceptual framework, including a useful flow-chart summarizing attack models and exploit types. The blog underscores the non-trivial nature of defenses, with most approaches failing in practice due to performance overheads, compatibility issues, or incomplete protection. The key insight is the categorization of attacks (code corruption, control-flow hijacking, data-only attacks, information leaking) and defenses, providing a structured understanding of this persistent security challenge.
